theorem_title: A smaller residue-20 ancestor from divisibility by the thirteenth power of three
natural_language_statement:
Let $T:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ be the shortcut Collatz map: $T(n)=n/2$ for even $n$ and $T(n)=(3n+1)/2$ for odd $n$. Write $T^k$ for its $k$-fold iterate, with $T^0(n)=n$.

Let $r\in\mathbb N$ satisfy $3^{13}\mid(4r+1)$. Then

$$
\exists m,b\in\mathbb N,\quad 0<m<r,\quad m\equiv20\pmod{27},\quad T^b(m)=r.
$$

The premise is only integer divisibility; a maximal power-of-three factorization is constructed within the proof. The divisor condition remains a genuine guard.
